JARVIS RESEARCH INSTITUTE
Founding Document  ·  JRI-001
Constitution  ·  Architecture  ·  Sprint-001 Delivery Plan
LG Jacques Pty Ltd  ·  August 2026
1.  System Overview
The Jarvis ecosystem consists of three independent projects with clearly separated responsibilities.
These three projects are related but never directly coupled. The only interface between them is the Proposal — a versioned, human-reviewed document that carries a research finding from JRI into the Genesis roadmap.
2.  JRI Constitution  v1.0
The Constitution is a permanent document. It does not change unless explicitly revised by the project owner. All JRI campaigns, experiments, and proposals operate under these principles regardless of how sophisticated JRI becomes.
Principle 8 — Knowledge expires unless revalidated — is the Confidence Decay rule. A lesson recorded in 2026 about Flask routing may be incorrect by 2028. Every knowledge entry carries a review_due date. Unreviewed knowledge degrades in confidence automatically. This prevents JRI from becoming a digital hoarder.
3.  Three-Project Architecture
3.1  Jarvis-OS
The production system. Genesis roadmap continues exactly as planned. JRI has no filesystem access to Jarvis-OS. The only input JRI can give Jarvis-OS is an approved Proposal, which a human then implements as a Genesis Sprint.
3.2  Jarvis Research
The active experimentation engine. Runs Campaigns. Produces Experiments, Benchmarks, and Research Papers. Writes Proposals. Reads Jarvis-OS via a thin read-only API client. Never writes to Jarvis-OS.
3.3  Jarvis Knowledge
The permanent institutional memory. Jarvis Research writes to it. Jarvis Research reads from it. Jarvis-OS never directly accesses it — knowledge flows through Proposals only.
4.  Jarvis Knowledge — Schema
Every knowledge entry is a structured record. This is not a note. It is a scientific knowledge item with provenance, confidence, and an expiry mechanism.
4.1  Negative Knowledge
Most systems record what worked. JRI explicitly preserves what failed. Negative Knowledge entries are first-class citizens — not bug reports, not deleted experiments. They are institutional memory.
When a future Campaign proposes the same idea, JRI can respond: "Campaign-003 already tested this. Here is why it failed." That prevents repeating expensive mistakes.
4.2  Confidence Decay
Knowledge does not age gracefully without intervention. Each domain carries a decay rate — the number of days before a knowledge entry's confidence begins to fall and a review is flagged.
5.  Research Workflow
6.  Research Roles
JRI is designed around roles rather than a single AI agent. Today, all roles may use the same underlying model. The role architecture exists so that future campaigns can assign specialised models per role without restructuring anything.
7.  The Proposal Engine
A Proposal is the only mechanism by which JRI influences Jarvis-OS. It is intentionally lightweight — an executive summary. The supporting detail lives in Knowledge Entries, Experiment records, and the Research Paper.
Proposals are versioned. A rejected proposal may be revised and resubmitted as a new version with additional evidence.
8.  Research Papers
Every completed Campaign produces one Research Paper. Papers are published to jarvis-knowledge/papers/ and are never deleted. They form the archive of Jarvis's evolution.
9.  Safety Rules — Hard Limits
These limits are permanent. They do not relax as JRI becomes more capable.
10.  Sprint-001 — Foundation Delivery Plan
Sprint-001 builds the framework only. Nothing is autonomous. Nothing modifies Jarvis-OS. Nothing writes proposals automatically. The goal is an elegant foundation that can evolve naturally over months.
Four internal sprints:
Sprint-001-A  —  Scaffold
•  Create jarvis-research/ and jarvis-knowledge/ directories
•  Create CONSTITUTION.md
•  Create config.py with ResearchConfig, trusted sources, decay rates
•  Create requirements.txt
Sprint-001-B  —  Core Models
•  Implement Experiment dataclass with JSON serialisation
•  Implement Proposal dataclass (full versioned schema)
•  Implement KnowledgeEntry dataclass with confidence decay
•  Unit tests for all three models
Sprint-001-C  —  Managers + Journal
•  Implement CampaignManager — load/save/list from campaigns/
•  Implement KnowledgeBase — write/read/search/decay-check
•  Implement ResearchJournal — append-only JSON log
•  Create CAMP-001.json (Conversation Intelligence campaign)
•  Unit tests
Sprint-001-D  —  Integration + Client
•  Implement ResearchManager as top-level coordinator
•  Implement JarvisClient with read-only HTTP calls
•  Wire everything through main.py
•  Full test suite green — 30+ passing, 0 failed
11.  Sprint-001 Success Criteria
Research is not measured by code written. It is measured by knowledge gained and infrastructure validated.
✓  jarvis-research/ runs standalone
✓  jarvis-knowledge/ directory structure in place
✓  CONSTITUTION.md committed and readable
✓  All models serialise to / from JSON
✓  KnowledgeBase persists entries across restarts
✓  Confidence decay calculates correctly
✓  ResearchJournal is append-only (no deletes possible)
✓  JarvisClient successfully calls Jarvis-OS /status
✓  Campaign-001 loads from CAMP-001.json
✓  Negative Knowledge entry can be created and queried
✓  Test suite: 30+ tests, 0 failed
✓  Jarvis-OS: completely untouched
"Jarvis-OS remains stable.  JRI remains fearless."
JRI Constitution v1.0  is in force from the first commit.
LG Jacques Pty Ltd  ·  Jarvis Research Institute  ·  August 2026

Implementation Plan

Key files to create/modify
- jarvis-research/ (package init)
- jarvis-research/config.py (ResearchConfig, decay rates, trusted sources)
- jarvis-research/models/experiment.py, proposal.py, knowledge_entry.py (dataclasses + JSON)
- jarvis-research/managers/campaign_manager.py, knowledge_base.py, research_manager.py
- jarvis-research/journal/research_journal.py (append-only)
- jarvis-research/client/jarvis_client.py (read-only HTTP)
- jarvis-research/main.py (wire-up)
- jarvis-research/tests/ (30+ unit tests)
- jarvis-research/campaigns/CAMP-001.json
- jarvis-knowledge/entries/, jarvis-knowledge/papers/, jarvis-knowledge/index.json
- CONSTITUTION.md
- requirements.txt
- .gitignore, pyproject.toml or setup.cfg (linters/formatters), README.md

Primary design decisions
- Strict three-project isolation; JRI communicates to Jarvis-OS via human-reviewed Proposals only.
- JSON as canonical storage; stable versioned schemas with migration hooks.
- Confidence Decay: per-domain decay rates; review_due enforcement and scheduled checks.
- Negative Knowledge as first-class with explicit failure_reason and context.
- ResearchJournal is append-only via write-once files plus hash chain for integrity.
- JarvisClient is read-only; base URL config-driven; retries and timeouts.
- Deterministic tests; filesystem mocked; no network in unit tests.

Risks
- Schema drift breaking backward compatibility; mitigate with versioning/migrations.
- Accidental write paths to Jarvis-OS; mitigate with client contract and tests.
- Clock skew impacting decay; mitigate with UTC and monotonic checks.
- Journal tampering; mitigate with hash chain and verification tests.

  "operations": []
}
